journeys.evidence_cell: Real pull + real run of `ghcr.io/ai-agent-assembly/aa-gateway:latest` (see J17 — same container, this journey's own ID). Container reached a healthy listening state, confirmed via `docker logs` and a real TCP connect from the host. Torn down after.

Original (struck through): registration-only smoke, no framework tool call attempted. **Full investigation (2026-08-23):** built the real, officially-documented path — published PyPI `agent-assembly==0.0.1rc6` (native `_core` extension present) + real `langchain`/`langchain-core` + a real standalone `aa-runtime` sidecar + real `aa-gateway`, all wired per `init_assembly(mode="sdk-only")` + `agent_assembly.adapters.langchain.AssemblyCallbackHandler` (a companion docs finding, AAASM-5836, was filed and then **retracted** the same day — a `WebFetch` summarization artifact, not a real docs defect). Result at the time: **every** governed LangChain tool call failed — including the canonical ALLOWED `read_file` action — with `ToolExecutionBlockedError('credential token registered to a different agent')`. Decisive isolating check: the Rust `e2e_runtime_gateway_deny` test (same runtime→gateway wire, bypassing Python) **passed**, proving the defect was specifically in the Python SDK's connection/credential-relay layer. **Filed as [AAASM-5835](https://lightning-dust-mite.atlassian.net/browse/AAASM-5835), High, confirmed defect; root-caused, fixed, tested (105/105 unit + 1/1 differential e2e), independently reviewed, merged to `main` at `79ac000f7db4fa27220ade16bbe39e123a26a5e0` (PR #2147), post-merge verified, Jira Done.** **Post-merge re-reproduction (2026-08-23) against the unchanged, currently-published PyPI wheel still fails identically** — expected, not a regression: that wheel's native extension is built from `python-sdk`'s `native/aa-ffi-python` crate, pinned to an old `aa-sdk-client` git SHA independent of this repo's `main`. This distribution gap is filed separately as **[AAASM-5839](https://lightning-dust-mite.atlassian.net/browse/AAASM-5839)** (`python-sdk`, High). **AAASM-5839's code-level fix is now also merged** (`python-sdk` PR #324) and end-to-end verified: a wheel built from the re-pinned `aa-ffi-python` against real `aa-gateway`/`aa-runtime` binaries reproduces the exact same scenario with `read_file` **executing** and `delete_file` **blocked** on a real policy decision — the strongest evidence available short of an actual PyPI release that the fix is complete. J56 AC #4 ("Execute the canonical ALLOWED action → succeeds") **still fails today for any real `pip install` user**, purely because that release has not shipped yet (out of this session's authority per Release Operations Policy) — not because of any remaining code defect.
journeys.evidence_ref: ~~CONFIRMED DEFECT (AAASM-5835)~~ → **FIXED UPSTREAM, STILL FAILS FOR PUBLISHED ARTIFACT (AAASM-5839)**

journeys.evidence_cell: Deploy/observe/govern legs PASS (unchanged). Original recover leg (struck through): **2 real defects found here** (AAASM-5832 / AAASM-5833). **Re-verification (2026-08-23):** both independently reproduced fixed against a locally built release `aasm` binary at `9c17c594a`. F-1: held port 18099 with a controlled Python listener (confirmed via `lsof` before launch), `aasm gateway start` correctly reported `error: aa-gateway (pid …) exited before becoming ready — it did not bind 127.0.0.1:18099`, exit code 1 (previously: false "started" + live PID). F-2: started a real gateway, `kill -9`'d its PID, confirmed via `ps -p` the process was gone, then `aasm gateway status` correctly reported `Gateway: not running (stale PID file — process … is no longer alive)`, exit code 1 (previously: false "pid exists but port is unreachable"). Recover leg now tells the truth; journey PASS.
